references.text: Pharaoh earlier admits his sin against the Lord during the hail plague, using similar words: 'This time I have sinned'
Pharaoh continues his confession and asks Moses for forgiveness of his sin
Shows the pattern where Pharaoh sins again after admitting his sin
Balaam uses a similar confession: 'I have sinned' (חָטָאתִי)
Saul confesses his sin with the same expression: 'I have sinned' (חָטָאתִי)
Saul repeats the confession 'I have sinned', but like Pharaoh, he shows no genuine repentance
David confesses 'I have sinned against the Lord' using the same Hebrew expression
Judas confesses 'I have sinned', but like Pharaoh, it does not lead to true repentance
The prodigal son plans to confess: 'I have sinned against heaven and against you'
The prodigal son confesses his sin, in contrast to Pharaoh's superficial confession
Contrast between God's requirement for humility (v.3) and Pharaoh's temporary fulfillment of this by admitting sin (v.16).
Theological contrast between Pharaoh's self-serving confession without repentance and Moses' willing sacrifice for the people's sin.
